risk: Synthetic dataset may not represent real banking traffic.
evidence: PaySim synthetic dataset; temporal and segment audits.
mitigation: Validate on representative, legally approved real transaction data before production use.
monitoring: Compare real transaction distributions, fraud prevalence, transaction types and account behaviour.

risk: CASH_OUT fraud detection is weak in the 50K-250K amount band.
evidence: 164 of 168 frauds in this test segment were missed; segment recall approximately 2.38%.
mitigation: Investigate segment-specific features and collect representative real-world cases. Do not change the frozen threshold using test data.
monitoring: Track CASH_OUT recall, alert rate and missed-fraud exposure by amount band when labels become available.

risk: Fraud prevalence and transaction mix vary substantially over time.
mitigation: Establish population, segment and label monitoring; review model validity when material changes occur.
monitoring: Track prevalence, transaction mix, feature PSI, segment-level performance and alert volumes.

risk: False negatives may involve substantial transaction amounts.
evidence: Neural model missed-fraud gross transaction amount was approximately $26.35M on the held-out synthetic test.
mitigation: Use exposure-weighted review and investigate high-risk missed-fraud segments. Gross amount is not confirmed bank loss.
monitoring: Track missed-fraud count, gross amount, amount distribution and confirmed financial loss separately.

risk: A frozen validation threshold may not remain suitable under changing prevalence.
evidence: Frozen threshold 0.1444527954; validation and test prevalence differ materially.
mitigation: Require formal approval, validation and versioning for any future threshold change. Never silently retune.
monitoring: Monitor alert rate, precision, recall and operational review capacity.

risk: SHAP explanations describe model behaviour, not causal drivers.
evidence: Grouped SHAP experiment; correlated numeric features can still produce unrealistic masked combinations.
mitigation: Treat explanations as diagnostic evidence; validate with domain experts and avoid causal claims.
monitoring: Review explanation stability and feature attribution changes across relevant segments.

risk: Invalid or malformed inputs may cause unsafe predictions.
evidence: Six input validation rejection tests passed in robustness testing.
mitigation: Enforce schema, finite numeric values, valid transaction type and feature ordering at every scoring boundary.
monitoring: Track rejected requests, schema failures, missing fields and invalid-value rates.

risk: Raw transaction balance equations may not reconcile.
evidence: Validation accounting audit found substantial residuals, especially for the origin-balance equation.
mitigation: Define transaction-type-specific accounting rules and investigate exceptions before treating residuals as errors.
monitoring: Track equation residual distributions and reconciliation failure rates by transaction type.

risk: No demonstrated production-grade monitoring and incident process yet.
evidence: Offline experiments and reports exist; live monitoring, on-call ownership and incident drills are not established.
mitigation: Build monitoring, alerting, runbooks, incident ownership and rollback procedures before a live pilot.
monitoring: Track service health, latency, failures, model version, data freshness and alert delivery.

risk: Production banking data may have privacy, retention and access constraints.
evidence: No production data governance or compliance approval has been established in this research project.
mitigation: Obtain legal, privacy, security and compliance review; minimise and protect sensitive data.
monitoring: Audit access, retention, encryption, data lineage and approved processing purposes.

risk: Model, feature transformation or threshold versions may become inconsistent.
evidence: Frozen model hash verification and validation reconciliation are implemented in experiments.
mitigation: Version model, feature schema, scaler, threshold and configuration as one approved release.
monitoring: Verify model hash and feature schema at startup and record versions with every prediction.

risk: Automated decisions may cause inappropriate customer impact.
evidence: Model produces REVIEW-style risk signals; production decision governance has not been established.
mitigation: Use human review for consequential actions; establish appeal, override and escalation processes.
monitoring: Track reviewer overrides, confirmed outcomes, complaints and decision turnaround times.
